access_model.notes: No internal configuration or status registers. One 8-bit port byte is written to drive outputs and read back as the port state.

preconditions: Use the configured 7-bit target address from address_rule.
For input mode, keep the corresponding port bits written high before using them as inputs.

transaction.notes: PCF8574 has no register pointer; the port byte is returned directly after the address phase.

steps.notes: Send start, target address with R/W=1, then read one byte containing P7..P0. Canonicalized from write_then_read with no pointer/payload bytes; the slave address byte is handled by the bus layer.
Decode returned byte bits as P7..P0. The same port byte also reflects the output latch/state for pins driven as outputs.

operation_flows.notes: Single-byte I2C access directly reads or writes the quasi-bidirectional port; no internal status/config registers exist.

steps.notes: Interrupt output asserts on any rising or falling edge of port inputs in input mode.

Interrupt is reset/reactivated when the port is read or written; during read mode the reset happens at the acknowledge bit after the rising edge of SCL, and in write mode at the acknowledge bit after the high-to-low transition of SCL.

operation_flows.notes: Interrupts that occur during the acknowledge clock pulse can be lost or very short due to resetting during this pulse.

steps.notes: Power-on reset is achieved by a power cycle; no bus transaction is required.

error_conditions.name: i2c_nack_on_address_or_data
error_conditions.condition: Target does not acknowledge the address byte or the data byte on write/read access.
error_conditions.driver_action: Abort the transaction and return an I/O error.
error_conditions.notes: After receiving the valid address byte, this device responds with an acknowledge; the data byte is followed by an acknowledge sent from this device.

error_conditions.name: interrupt_lost_during_ack_pulse
error_conditions.condition: An interrupt occurs during the acknowledge clock pulse while the interrupt circuit is being reset.
error_conditions.driver_action: Accept that the edge may be lost; if the application requires edge capture, poll the port state after the read/write transaction.
error_conditions.notes: Interrupts that occur during the acknowledge clock pulse can be lost (or be very short).

error_conditions.name: port_access_with_invalid_bus_sequence
error_conditions.condition: Driver attempts to address a nonexistent register pointer or send extra bytes expecting internal register auto-increment.
error_conditions.driver_action: Abort the operation and treat the access model as a direct single-byte port transfer only.
error_conditions.notes: This device does not have internal configuration or status registers.

evidence_spans.snippet: This device does not have internal configuration or status registers. Instead, read or write to the device I/Os directly after sending the device address
The data byte follows the address acknowledge. If the R/ W bit is high, the data from this device are the values read from the P port.
If the R/ W bit is low, the data are from the controller, to be output to the P port.
An interrupt is generated by any rising or falling edge of the port inputs in the input mode.
Resetting occurs in the read mode at the acknowledge bit after the rising edge of the SCL signal
At power on, the I/Os are high.
Power-on reset requires that the device go through a power cycle to be completely reset.
V POR is the voltage level at which the reset condition is released and all the registers and the I 2 C/SMBus state machine are initialized to their default states.

requires_human: The datasheet uses 8-bit write/read address tables; the IR normalizes them to 7-bit addresses 0x20..0x27. Please confirm the host stack expects 7-bit I2C addresses, not wire-byte addresses.

The interrupt clear sequence is described in terms of acknowledge timing; confirm whether the implementation should also explicitly read back the port byte after an interrupt to avoid missing short pulses.

The datasheet says all I/Os are high at power on, but it does not provide a byte-level reset latch value beyond the pin-state description; confirm whether software should treat the default port byte as 0xFF.
